description: Three-tier string architecture with full Unicode correctness: inline (0-7 bytes), interned flat (8-128 bytes), rope (129+ bytes). NFD normalization, grapheme-based length/index/slice, hash-accelerated rope equality.

userStories.notes: The existing utf8_find_safe_split (unicode.h:140) only walks back past continuation bytes (0x80-0xBF). The function must handle the case where walking back reaches position 0 (return 0). ROPE_LEAF_MAX is 256 bytes (rope.h:50). The change in rope_from_str is a single-line replacement at line 130: change utf8_find_safe_split to grapheme_find_safe_split. userStories.title: rope_concat grapheme boundary invariant
userStories.description: As the rope implementation, I need rope_concat to enforce that no grapheme cluster spans the junction between two concatenated ropes.
acceptanceCriteria: After rope_concat joins two ropes, check if the right tree's leftmost leaf starts with codepoints that have Extend/ZWJ/SpacingMark grapheme break property
If combining codepoints are found at the start of the right side, move those bytes from the right's leftmost leaf to the left's rightmost leaf
Affected leaf summaries are recomputed via rope_summary_summarize()
The fix-up only triggers when the right side starts with combining characters (O(1) check by decoding first codepoint)
If the right's leftmost leaf becomes empty after moving bytes, it is removed
If the left's rightmost leaf overflows ROPE_LEAF_MAX after receiving bytes, it is re-split using grapheme_find_safe_split
Unit tests: rope_concat where right rope is just combining marks (e.g., U+0301 U+0327) — bytes move to left
Unit tests: rope_concat where right starts with a base character — no fix-up, counts sum correctly
Unit tests: repeated concat operations maintain the invariant (no accumulated grapheme count drift)
Unit tests: rope grapheme count after concat matches unicode_grapheme_count on materialized flat string
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: rope_concat is in lib/sum_tree/rope.h. The rope is a persistent data structure (RC-based), so modifying a leaf requires creating new nodes up to the root — this is standard for persistent trees and costs O(log n). The implementation approach: after rope_st_concat, access the leftmost leaf of the right subtree and the rightmost leaf of the left subtree. Scan the right leaf's prefix for extending codepoints. If found, create a new right leaf without those bytes and a new left leaf with those bytes appended. Use rope_st_mk_leaf to create new leaves. The rope uses RC (reference counting) — use rc_retain/rc_release as needed. The combining-mark check uses unicode_grapheme_break() — GBP_EXTEND, GBP_ZWJ, GBP_SPACINGMARK indicate non-starter codepoints.

Workflow: (1) validate UTF-8, (2) check unicode_is_nfd — if true, skip normalization, (3) call unicode_nfd_length to get output size, (4) allocate buffer (stack for small, arena for large), (5) call unicode_nfd. userStories.title: Grapheme-based index across all tiers
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want [index s i] to return the i-th grapheme cluster so indexing aligns with visible characters.

[index s i] where i is negative or >= grapheme length returns nil
For inline/flat strings: linear scan through grapheme clusters using unicode grapheme iteration (O(n), bounded at 128 bytes)

Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: The current index builtin in vm.c does byte-based indexing. Change it to grapheme-based. For inline/flat strings: iterate through the bytes counting grapheme clusters using the grapheme break algorithm from unicode.h. When you reach the i-th cluster, extract its bytes (from cluster start to next cluster start). For rope strings: use rope_cursor_advance_graphemes(cursor, i) to seek to the right position, then extract the bytes of the current grapheme cluster. The grapheme iteration uses unicode_grapheme_break() to detect cluster boundaries — a new cluster starts when the break algorithm says 'break here'. Helper function suggestion: jacl_grapheme_nth(const uint8_t* data, size_t len, size_t n, size_t* out_start, size_t* out_end) — finds byte range of nth grapheme.

userStories.notes: The current OP_CONCAT in vm.c handles inline+inline and inline+heap combinations. Extend it for all 9 combos. Strategy: (1) compute total byte length from both operands, (2) if total ≤128: extract bytes from both into a stack buffer, pass to jacl_string_new() — this handles inline/flat routing and interning, (3) if total >128: convert both operands to ropes (non-rope operands via rope_from_str on their bytes), then rope_concat — the rope_concat invariant from US-002 handles grapheme boundaries, wrap result in JaclRopeString. For extracting bytes: use jacl_string_data() for inline/flat, rope_to_str() for rope. For the grapheme boundary check on flat results: check if right operand's first byte starts a combining codepoint — if so, recompute grapheme count on the concatenated buffer instead of summing. For rope results, US-002's rope_concat handles this automatically.
